sources.citation: Lovestrand, Joseph, Misriani Balle & Owen Edwards. 2022. Notes on Kodi Phonology. Journal of the Southeast Asian Linguistics Society 15.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Only full phonological description (with a stress section and measured stress-induced vowel lengthening) of the closest relative, Kodi; may contain a remark on Garo/Gaura. Not a Garo description, but the reference point if the catalog ever accepts a Kodi proxy or a note on the Kodi-Gaura pair.

sources.citation: Balle, Misriani & Joseph Lovestrand. 2019. Sumba wordlists and phrases. PARADISEC collection JL4.
sources.note: Primary audio wordlists of West Sumba languages collected by the Kodi phonology team; if it holds a Gaura list, it is the only primary phonetic data on the language (stress could be read off recordings, not a published statement).

sources.citation: Lovestrand, Joseph. 2021. Languages of Sumba: State of the field. NUSA: Linguistic studies of languages in and around Indonesia 70: 39-60. doi:10.15026/100089
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Survey, not a description of Gaura. p.43: Gaura is 'a distinct language of West Sumba', known only lexically (Asplund 2010; Gasser 2014); p.52 lists 'the status of Gaura as a separate language' as an open research need. The only stress remark (sec. 4.2, p.48) is about Kodi and Weyewa: 'Weyewa and Kodi have contrastive long consonants, and non-contrastive lengthening of stressed vowels—typically the penultimate syllable (Kuipers 1998:xvii; Lovestrand & Balle 2019)', with Kodi examples [ˈpoːto] 'four', [ˈpotːo]. Nothing on Gaura stress.

sources.citation: Ghanggo Ate, Yustinus. 2020. Kodi (Indonesia) — Language Snapshot. Language Documentation and Description 19: 171-180. doi:10.25894/ldd77
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No stress statement. p.174: Ethnologue's three Kodi dialects (Kodi Bokolo, Kodi Bangedo, 'Garo or Nggaro') reduced to two, 'while Garo is a separate language'; Kodi examples carry penultimate stress marks ([ˈwaːtaro] 'corn', [paˈhondoŋo]) but nothing is said about stress placement, and nothing about Garo phonology. downloaded from the the Internet Archive snapshot 2026-01-14 (publisher site is behind an Anubis bot challenge).

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page 'Garo (Sumba)' ngga1239 (Hammarström et al.), with subclassification comment citing Asplund 2010:9, Gasser 2014, Ghanggo Ate 2020:174, Lovestrand 2021:43, Eberhard et al. 2022
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No descriptive reference at all (Glottolog lists no grammar, sketch or phonology). Comment: listed as a third dialect of Kodi [kod] in Ethnologue E16-E28, 'However, all reports suggest a lack of inherent intelligibility between Garo and Kodi.. and the lexicostatistical figures are more consistent with two different languages'. Alternative names Gaura, Nggaura.
